note: Derived from the existing app data by word-aligning vocalized Hebrew to the Georgian text with a DP aligner (see KA-NOTES.md). Keys are Hebrew letter/point NAMES. Every phoneme entry has up to three evidence blocks: A = baseline system (Torah+Targum, Tehillim, Rambam, Zohar, Daf, Chok LeYisrael weekly texts, Tanya), P = prayers-ka.json, B = Ben Ish Chai. "n" = occurrences (token-weighted); "dist" = share of each realisation; examples are {he,ka} from the data.

A.role: BASELINE - ~98% of all aligned tokens; internally consistent (looks machine-generated by one rule set)

P.role: prayers/siddur; differs from A (k-sounds, tet, he)

B.role: Ben Ish Chai halachot; differs from A (k-sounds, p, b/v, tet, final he) and contains Latin-letter contamination

engineMaps.description: flat baseline (system A = current dominant behaviour) mapping, ready for a language module. Names are Hebrew letter/point names.

shva-na.note: derived: A,P,B all write ე for every shva the engine classifies as na; see shvaContexts for how often each context is vocalised

rules.rule: Dagesh chazak (dagesh after a vowel) DOUBLES the consonant letter: ל->ლლ, מ->მმ, נ->ნნ, ש->შშ, ס->სს, ז->ზზ, צ->წწ, ט->ტტ, ק->კკ, ו->ვვ, י->იი and the begedkefet letters ბბ/გგ/დდ/კკ/პპ/თთ.
rules.evidence: A: non-begedkefet after vowel 99.5% doubled (n=240,507), begedkefet after vowel 97.9% (n=171,070); B 99.3%/99.9%; P 79%/95%.

rules.rule: Dagesh kal (begedkefet at word start, or after a silent shva) is NOT doubled.
rules.evidence: A: word-initial 100% single (n=486,385); after shva 100% single (n=68,350). B 96-100%.

rules.rule: Shva na -> ე; shva nach -> silent. Observed ე share: word-initial 100%, after another shva 91.5%, after shuruk 93.6%, after a short vowel 15.7%, after a long vowel 2.6%. The 15.7% after short vowels is mostly a shva under a letter carrying dagesh chazak (הַדְּבָרִים->ჰადდევარიმ, אִתְּתָא->ითთეთა) and some letter-specific cases (הַכְנָסָה->ჰახენასა); the exact generator rule is not recoverable.
rules.evidence: SHVA contexts in shvaContexts block (A n=1,058,607 shvas).

rules.rule: Chataf-patach -> ა, chataf-segol -> ე, chataf-qamatz -> ო (no extra shva sound). Aleph/ayin carrying a chataf do not double the vowel: אֲשֶׁר->აშერ, יַעֲקֹב->იააკოვ (the ა after ი is the patach of yod + the chataf of ayin).
rules.evidence: 100% in all three systems (A n=151,840 chataf-patach).

rules.rule: Aleph and ayin are never written as consonants (no apostrophe, no ა-glottal); they only carry their vowel. 552,246 aleph and 244,824 ayin in A: 100% silent. Apostrophes do not occur in transliterated tokens at all.

He is ჰ when it carries a vowel, is mid-word, or has mappiq. Final he WITHOUT mappiq is silent in A after qamatz/patach/segol/tsere/cholam (87-100%): תּוֹרָה->თორა, מֹשֶׁה->მოშე. Mappiq he is written ჰ: לָהּ->ლაჰ, אֵינָהּ->ენაჰ. System B writes final he as ჰ after segol/tsere (100%) and mostly after qamatz-gadol only 11%; P is mixed 70-95% silent.

Consonantal vav -> ვ (וַ->ვა, וְ->ვე). Shuruk (vav+dagesh, no vowel) -> უ (vav itself silent). Cholam male (ו with ֹ) -> ო (vav silent). Vav after qamatz/patach word-finally (עֵשָׂו, צַו) -> ვ. Doubled vav-with-dagesh -> ვვ.

Yod that carries a vowel or dagesh is ALWAYS ი, so initial יִ gives იი (יִשְׂרָאֵל->იისრაელ) and yod+dagesh+chirik gives იიი (חַיִּים->ხაიიიმ). Mater yod after chirik / tsere / segol (medial) is silent. Yod after patach or qamatz at word end is ი (אֵלַי->ელაი, אֲדֹנָי->ადონაი); after cholam word-final ი (גּוֹי->გოი). Medial patach+yod+consonant is ი (ai) and იი when the yod has dagesh (הַיּוֹם->ჰაიიომ). The sequence ָיו is written ავ (yod silent): עָלָיו->ალავ.
rules.evidence: matresLectionis yod|*; A: 17,713 tokens begin with იი, 13,932 contain იიი, 748 contain იიიი
rules.confidence: high (current behaviour) but flagged as awkward - see KA-NOTES

rules.rule: Qamatz gadol -> ა. Qamatz katan -> ო (word list needed: כָּל/כׇּל->კოლ, חׇכְמָה, שׇׁרְשׁ...). In A 97.6% of all qamatz are ა; 2.4% are ო because the sources contain qamatz katan, mostly כָּל written with a plain qamatz.
rules.confidence: medium - the engine needs the same qamatz-katan detection

rules.rule: Final letter forms are written exactly like the non-final letter: ך->ხ (A) / ქ (P,B), ם->მ, ן->ნ, ף->ფ, ץ->წ. Final kaf with shva is silent-vowel: לָךְ->ლახ.

Maqaf -> hyphen "-" (Torah 11,765 hyphens vs 11,474 maqafs; Tehillim 2,500 vs 2,468). Sof pasuk -> ":" in Torah (5,836) but NOT in Tehillim (no punctuation at all). No apostrophes, no hyphen inside a word except for maqaf, no diacritics. Cantillation and nikud are never reproduced.

The Tetragrammaton in every spelling (יְהֹוָה, יְיָ, ה׳, ה', יי) and אֲדֹנָי are all written ადონაი. The word השם (HaShem) is written ჰაშშემ (176) rarely ჰაშემ (4). אֱלֹהִים->ელოჰიმ, אֱלֹהֵינוּ->ელოჰენუ.

Only the 24 lower-case Mkhedruli letters ა ბ გ დ ე ვ ზ თ ი კ ლ მ ნ ო პ რ ს ტ უ ფ შ ხ ჰ წ (24 letters) are used by system A; ქ appears only in P/B and ც only in titles/UI. NEVER used anywhere in body text: ღ ყ ძ ჟ ჩ ჭ ჯ, and ც/ქ are absent from system A.
rules.evidence: letter frequency over ~18M characters of A text

divineName.note: identical in A, P, B. UI strings also use ჰაშემ for יהוה (ლედავიდ ჰაშემ ორი = לדוד יהוה אורי) - an inconsistency with the body.

uiTerms.forbidden: პარაშა (slang) - 0 occurrences as a section name in index.html/prayers-ka; the only hits in torah-ka.json are the unrelated Aramaic words פָּרָשָׁיו/פַּרְשָׁיָא
uiTerms.construct: ფარაშათ (1 UI string: פרשת => ფარაშათ, + "ფარაშათ ჰათამიდ")

punctuation.note: Torah ka: 11,765 hyphens vs 11,474 maqaf; 5,836 colons vs 5,853 sof-pasuk; Tehillim ka: only hyphens (2,500). Rambam/Zohar/Daf/Leyisrael keep Hebrew-source punctuation (":", ".", "(", ")", quotes) token-by-token.

latinLettersInsideGeorgianWords.note: Latin a/e/i/o/u inside Georgian words (homoglyph-style corruption); renders in a different font and breaks copy/search.

mtavruli.where: chok-daf (18,972 tokens), chok-leyisrael (1,093), BIC (2,310), few elsewhere
mtavruli.note: word-initial Mtavruli capitals (e.g. Ამარ, Ვეჰა, Ქi) vs lower-case for the same word elsewhere; Torah/Tehillim/prayers have none.

scriptHygiene.htmlInTokens: rare fragments like "ლო" and "ბარეხ" appear where source strings contain markup (chok-leyisrael/chok-daf/chok-rambam)
scriptHygiene.mixedScript: Torah ka is clean: 0 Latin, 0 Mtavruli.

openQuestions: Which of the three existing systems is the intended canonical one? A (Torah/Tehillim/Rambam/Zohar/Daf/Chok/Tanya, ~98% of text) differs from P (prayers) and B (Ben Ish Chai) in 7 consonant/vowel choices - see divergences in KA-NOTES.md.
Kaf-with-dagesh and qof are merged into ONE letter in every system (A: კ, P/B: ქ). No system keeps them apart. Is the merge acceptable for Georgian readers? (RECOMMENDATION: ქ for כּ, კ for ק.)

Tsadi: body text uses წ (ejective) everywhere (A 100%), but every title/UI name uses ც (ნიცავიმ, ვაიცე, თეცავე, მეცორა, ცომ). Which letter do community sources actually use for צ? Needs a Georgian-Hebrew speaker.
Pe-with-dagesh: A uses პ, but P, B and every UI title use ფ (ფეკუდე, ფინხას, ფურიმი, ფეთახ ელიაჰუ). Same question.
Tet: A uses ტ, P and B use თ (merging tet and tav). Recommended A (ტ for ט, თ for ת).
Bet-rafe: A ვ (200k), P ვ 78%/ბ 22%, B always ბ (merges bet/vet). Recommended A.

Doubled letters (gemination): the body text doubles every dagesh chazak (98-100% in A/B), the titles never do (ხაიე, ვაიკრა, თეჰილიმ, ხანუქა, ნიცავიმ). Owner note says community spellings avoid doubling - the engine needs one decision; spec encodes BOTH (flag geminate:true|false).
yod: initial/after-vowel yod+chirik is written იი and yod+dagesh+chirik იიი (13,932 A tokens, 748 with იიიი). Community forms are ისრაელ, ხაიმ, ვაიკრა. Confirm collapse to single ი.
Final he without mappiq: A silent, B always ჰ (ზეჰ, ბეჰ, ჰინნეჰ). Choose; recommended A (silent) with ჰ for mappiq.
Aleph/ayin carrying chataf-patach after patach gives a doubled ა (იააკოვ, ბააწათ, თააბბედ). Is יַעֲקֹב better as იაკოვ?

Qamatz katan has no marker in the Hebrew source except a few explicit ׇ (U+05C7) points; A writes ო for כָּל etc. The engine core needs its own qamatz-katan list; how complete was the one used for the existing data is unknown (2.4% of A qamatz are ო).

Shva na vs nach: the existing data vocalises ~15.7% of shvas after a short vowel (mostly under dagesh-chazak letters) and ~32% of shvas before an identical letter, 6.4% of shvas after shuruk are silent. The generator rule is not documented; engine will not match 100% here.
Segol/tsere + yod (אֵין, בֵּית, אֱלֹהֶיךָ): A writes ე (ენ, ბეთ, ელოხეხა) while the UI title בית יעקב is ბეით იაკოვ. Is ეი wanted for tsere-yod?
The letters ღ ყ ძ ჟ ჩ ჭ ჯ never occur in transliteration (A: 0 of ~18M chars). Should ჩ/ჭ/ჯ/ჟ (Hebrew צ׳/ג׳/ז׳/ת׳ in Judeo-Arabic loan words) be supported?
Capitalisation: lower-case only is used for Torah/Tehillim/prayers; Mtavruli initials appear in Daf/Leyisrael/BIC. Recommended lower-case only.
Latin-letter contamination in BIC (22,042 tokens): data-cleanup task, not a spec question, but the corpus excludes those tokens.
Whether ხ is right for BOTH ח and rafe-כ (merged in all three systems) or whether ჰ should mark ח. No evidence of any ჰ for chet; merging is consistent everywhere.
No native speaker reviewed: every claim above is a description of existing app behaviour, not of correct Georgian Jewish usage.

recommended.status: RECOMMENDATION - not evidence. Choose per the owner brief (community-aligned titles, Georgian readers). Flag-driven: an engine may expose `scheme:"current"|"recommended"`.

gemination.note: one letter for dagesh chazak (ლ not ლლ, ბ not ბბ).

recommended.verifiedAgainstTitles: with the overrides above the 8 reviewed names reproduce: ხაიე (חַיֵּי: yod+tsere, no doubling), ბერეშით, შემოთ, ვაიკრა, ბემიდბარ, ნიცავიმ, ხანუქა, თეჰილიმ.
